claims.text: A graphene-reinforced Ni-based composite coating can provide wide-temperature self-lubrication while retaining strong mechanical strength.
A Ni-based superalloy is a high-strength substrate.
The initial substrate has moderate wear resistance and tribological performance.
Graphene nanoplatelets can be uniformly dispersed within a Ni-based coating matrix.
The proposed coating can operate from room temperature to approximately 600°C.
The proposed coating can function in both dry and moderately lubricated environments.
Uniform graphene distribution enhances lubrication by enabling easy shear between graphene layers.
Uniformly distributed graphene reinforces the Ni matrix through load-sharing.
Graphene's layered structure produces a low-friction interface through facile interlayer sliding.
Graphene integrated into a Ni matrix blocks crack propagation.
Graphene integrated into a Ni matrix distributes stresses.
Crack blocking and stress distribution maintain coating structural stability at elevated temperatures.
The graphene-reinforced coating will have a lower coefficient of friction than an unreinforced Ni-based coating.
The graphene-reinforced coating will have a lower wear rate than an unreinforced Ni-based coating.
The graphene-reinforced coating will have greater mechanical strength than an unreinforced Ni-based coating across the tested temperature range.
Bare substrates and Ni-based coatings without graphene typically exhibit higher friction, higher wear, and degraded high-temperature performance.
Above approximately 600°C, oxidation or degradation of graphene or other coating constituents may limit the coating's benefits.
